title: Social Security Legislation Amendment (Technical Changes) Bill 2025
short_title: Social Security Legislation Amendment (Technical Changes) Bill 2025

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would create different payment rates for disability support pension recipients under 21 based on their living situation.
It would set a lower rate for those living with a parent and a higher rate for those living independently, matching longstanding policy.
The bill also confirms that rates for youth recipients do not depend on full-time study or apprenticeship status, and validates past rate decisions.
changes: Creates different disability support pension rates for recipients under 21 depending on their circumstances.
Sets a lower rate for dependent youth living at home and a higher rate for independent youth.
Removes the effect of full-time study or apprenticeship status on youth disability support pension rates.
Validates past rate decisions for youth recipients that were based on the dependent rate.
summary.affected: Disability support pension recipients under 21 and the Department of Social Services.

Those changes introduced the partial-capacity-to-work rule to the independence criteria, which was intended to apply to youth allowance recipients only. It's now understood that a drafting error in the 2005 amendments means that certain DSP recipients under 21 are impacted. This in turn affected the rates of support those recipients were entitled to receive. It would have added the text below to the usual second reading motion, which is "that the bill be read a second time" (which is parliamentary jargon for agreeing with the main idea of the bill). ### Amendment text > *At the end of the motion, add ", but the Senate:* > > *(a) notes that:* > >> *(i) the Disability Support Pension (DSP) partner income test traps disabled people in abusive relationships by forcing people into a dynamic of financial dependency,* >> >> *(ii) the DSP partner income test also prevents members of the community from forming relationships and getting married, and genuine marriage and partner equality must include the abolition of the partner income test,* >> >> *(iii) the low rate of the DSP forces many disabled people in vicious cycles of poverty, fear and pain,* >> >> *(iv) the tightening of eligibility of the DSP forces many people living with disability to rely on the lower rate under JobSeeker, entrenching poverty and disadvantage,* >> >> *(v) poverty is a political choice; and* > > *(b) calls on the Government to:* > >> *(i) abolish the punitive partner income test for the DSP, and* >> >> *(ii) raise the rate of income support payments as a matter of urgency".*
